title: DVR etale local equations for an at-worst-nodal curve
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with a chosen uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose each nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension], and each nonsmooth point has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring $\Omega[[a,b]]/(ab)$ over the algebraically closed geometric residue field $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For every point $x$ of the special fibre there exist a discrete valuation ring $R'$, an injective local etale map $R\to R'$ for which the image of $\pi$ is a uniformizer, an $R'$-scheme $U$, a point $u\in U$ above $x$, and etale $S$-morphisms $U\to X$ and $U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, where either $A=R'[a,b]/(ab)$ or $A=R'[a,b]/(ab-\pi^n)$ for an integer $n\geq0$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The maps to $S$ are induced by the stated $R'$-structures. If the generic fibre $X_K$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, is smooth, the zero-parameter model is unnecessary: at a nonsmooth $x$ the model may be chosen with $n\geq1$. No quasi-compactness, excellence, completeness, or residue-field perfection is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal). The fixed uniformizer of R can be used in R′ because a local etale extension of DVRs has maximal ideal generated by its image; the unit in the smoothing parameter is absorbed in one coordinate, as in the final paragraph of the proof. The smooth-generic refinement is the first paragraph of Tag 0CDE (lemma-blowup-at-worst-nodal), before any blowup is constructed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-nodal-etale-local-form] at $x$. Its hypotheses are exactly the flatness, local finite presentation and geometric nodal-curve hypotheses here (our condition at all nonsmooth geometric points includes its condition at closed ones). Obtain $R\hookrightarrow R'$, $p:U\to X$, $q:U\to W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $u$ above $x$, with the indicated compatible structural maps and either $A=R'[a_0,b_0]/(a_0b_0)$ or $A=R'[a_0,b_0]/(a_0b_0-(\pi')^n)$. An extension of DVRs is local: the maximal ideal of $R'$ contracts to that of $R$. Thus this supplies the required injective local etale map, without any quasi-compactness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, statement; local DVR extension as defined in more-algebra.tex, definition-extension-discrete-valuation-rings

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal] to $R\to R'$ and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_{R'}$. Its preimage is $\mathfrak m_R$ by locality, and $R'_{\mathfrak q}=R'$ because $R'$ is local (every inverted element is already a unit). Therefore $\mathfrak m_{R'}=\mathfrak m_R R'=(\pi)$. By the definition of uniformizer in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], the image of the originally chosen $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $R'$.

Since $(\pi')=(\pi)$ in the domain $R'$, write $\pi'=\epsilon\pi$ with $\epsilon\in(R')^\times$: the two divisibilities give $\pi'=c\pi$, $\pi=d\pi'$, hence $dc=1$ by cancellation of nonzero $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. In the nonzero-parameter model put $a=\epsilon^{-n}a_0$, $b=b_0$; then $ab=\pi^n$. Explicitly the isomorphism $R'[a,b]/(ab-\pi^n)\to R'[a_0,b_0]/(a_0b_0-(\pi')^n)$ sends $a\mapsto\epsilon^{-n}a_0$, $b\mapsto b_0$, with inverse $a_0\mapsto\epsilon^n a$, $b_0\mapsto b$. Compose $q$ with its spectrum isomorphism; an isomorphism is an open immersion, so this preserves etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The zero-parameter model is unchanged. This proves the first assertion with the fixed uniformizer.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, final paragraph, unit absorption with the coordinate maps written explicitly

proof.text: For either equation $ab=h$ over $R'$, its open $D(a)$ has coordinate ring $R'[a,a^{-1}]$ by eliminating $b=h/a$; likewise on $D(b)$. These opens are smooth over $R'$ directly from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: the presentation $R'[t,s]/(ts-1)$ is finite, and a map to $B/I$, $I^2=0$, lifts by choosing a lift of the image of $t$, which is a unit. Indeed, if lifts $t_0,s_0$ satisfy $t_0s_0=1+i$ with $i\in I$, replace $s_0$ by $s_0(1-i)$. This proves the required infinitesimal lifting. The model $ab=1$ is entirely such an open, since $a$ is invertible everywhere.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, smooth case and the displayed models; direct infinitesimal calculation using more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H0, definition-formally-smooth

proof.text: The etale map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Composing with the smooth opens of step 4 gives smoothness over $S$ by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Apply the pointwise equivalence in [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] first to $q$ and then to $p$, both over $S$. If $x$ is nonsmooth, $w=q(u)$ cannot belong to $D(a)\cup D(b)$, and the model cannot have $n=0$. Since $u$ lies over the closed point of $S$ and the extension $R\to R'$ is local, $w$ is then the origin $(\pi,a,b)$ of the special fibre. In particular, in a nonzero-parameter model at nonsmooth $x$, necessarily $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, smooth case; Tag 0CDE, first paragraph of proof; descent.tex Tag 036U, lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source

proof.text: In the zero-parameter model let $z=(a,b)\in\operatorname{Spec}(R'[a,b]/(ab))$, the generic point of its section $a=b=0$. It lies over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ because $R\hookrightarrow R'$ is injective. This generic-fibre point is not smooth over $K$, by the lifting definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}R'$, $B=F[e]/(e^3)$ and $I=(e^2)$, so $I^2=0$. The $K$-map from the model ring to $B/I$ sending $a,b\mapsto e$ and coefficients through $R'\to F$ has no lift to $B$: any lifts of $a,b$ have product $e^2\ne0$. This also tests every open neighbourhood of $z$, since the one-point spectra of $B/I$ and $B$ map to $z$.

source.place: Tag 0CDE, proof, the omitted detail excluding the persistent-node model; direct first-order lifting obstruction, more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H0

proof.text: Assume $X_K$ is smooth. If a zero-parameter chart has $w\in D(a)\cup D(b)$, restrict $U$ to the inverse image of one such open containing $u$. The new map to $X$ is etale by the open-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; the map to the chosen model open is the etale base change of $q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The chosen open is $\operatorname{Spec}R'[t,t^{-1}]\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R'[a,b]/(ab-1)$, so it gives the required $n=0$ model. Otherwise $w=(\pi,a,b)$. The map $q$ is open: etale means flat and locally finitely presented [def-weil-etale-morphism], and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] applies. Its open image contains $w$ and therefore its generization $z=(a,b)$. Choose $v\in U$ mapping to $z$; it lies in $U_K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], both $p_K:U_K\to X_K$ and $q_K:U_K\to W_K$ are etale. The pointwise equivalence [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness], with base $\operatorname{Spec}K$, makes $U_K$ smooth at $v$ from $X_K$, then makes $W_K$ smooth at $z$ from $U_K$. This contradicts step 6. Thus the zero-parameter case can always be replaced or excluded. At nonsmooth $x$, step 5 additionally excludes $n=0$, leaving $n\geq1$. All restrictions contain the chosen point and preserve the required maps; none uses excellence, completeness or residue-field perfection.
